newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's Saddam says U.S. worst dictator in world.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Saddam says U.S. worst dictator in world.

text.p: President Saddam Hussein, in remarks published on Wednesday, called the United States the worst despot history had ever known.

"There is despotism within known circles and in the forefront of the march towards the evil is America," the papers qouted Saddam as telling a delegation of foreign politicians led by former Algerian president Ahmed Ben Bella.
"They (Americans) wanted to impose a world order...but they were the worst dictators humanity has ever known," Saddam said.

Iraqi television late on Tuesday showed Saddam receiving a delegation which an announcer said was part of a Madrid- based gathering set up in 1996 to sue the United States and the U.N. Security Council for hardships emanating from the U.N. embargo imposed on Iraq for invading Kuwait in 1990.

The delegation handed Saddam the verdict, which accused the permanent members of the U.N. Security Council, particularly the United States, as well as Rolf Ekeus head of the U.N. Special Commission on Iraq, of genocide.
The curbs on Iraqi oil exports can only be lifted when Ekeus testifies to the Security Council that all Iraq's lethal weapons were either destroyed or rendered harmless.
Saddam said Iraq's survival in the face of the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait and the U.N. trade sanctions had disgraced the United States and its allies.
He said the U.S. was trying to extend its dictatorship to include the world at large, imposing its despotism on other people's governments, economies and way of living.
"Is there a dictatorship which is more vicious than this one (U.S.)?" Saddam asked.
